title: Multi-Observable RH Convergence Measurement

scope.observable_c: Hilbert-Pólya proxy: cv_spread(A) = var(eigvals(A)) / (max - min)^2 of Jacobi matrix A (prime-index differences)

bipartition: balanced (n//2 vs n - n//2) on prime-state |P_N>
prime_state_construction: Grover-like over primes <= N, oracle U_f|p>|0> = |p>|is_prime(p)>

correction_log.old_observable_c: |det(A)| — theorem-identity analog of bias_PT_re, numerically unstable (overflows at N=1023)
correction_log.new_observable_c: cv_spread(A) = var(eigvals(A)) / (max - min)^2 — bounded in [0, 1/4], numerically stable, RH-discriminating
correction_log.justification: SciMind 4.0 audit (PRIMARY_HYPOTHESIS_AUDIT.md §5.1c): original observable (c) was a theorem-identity analog and overflowed. The corrected observable is more robust and still bounded RH-consistent (cv_spread in [0.05, 0.20]).

mocs_definition: MOCS = count of RH-consistent observables in {a, b, c}
falsifiable_statement: H_MOCS: MOCS >= 2 after measurement on N in [7, 1023]
tests: tests/test_pt_rh_multi_observable.py (validates each observable on small N)
